positioning_statement: 8MSolar is an engineering-grade partner — not just a contractor who installs solar — that designs, installs, monitors, and guarantees systems for decades. Differentiation comes from in-house Chapter 87 professional engineers, hardware-agnostic equipment choice, and #1-by-volume installation data in NC, verified by a third party (Solar Power World Online).

named_competitors.name: Southern Energy Management (SEM)
named_competitors.notes: Credible NC competitor without an in-house Chapter 87 engineering license. Article tone: acknowledge SEM as credible, then let the credentials gap do the persuading — never a takedown.

named_competitors.name: NC Solar Now
named_competitors.notes: Closer competitor — both Raleigh-based, both Chapter 87 licensed, both NABCEP certified. Differentiation has to come from operational depth (full-time in-house PE) and third-party-verified installation volume (8,414 kW vs 5,828 kW, Solar Power World Online 2025), not credentials alone.

named_competitors.name: Yes Solar Solutions
named_competitors.notes: Smaller by volume (1,942 kW, 2019 — their most recent public figure) but holds genuine NABCEP company accreditation. Differentiation angle: service bandwidth/company longevity for post-installation support, and manufacturer-warranty-survival risk (hardware-agnostic vs. single-manufacturer lock-in).

named_competitors.name: Renu Energy Solutions
named_competitors.notes: Charlotte-based (8MSolar is Raleigh-based) — geographically distinct market. 6,630 kW installed (2024) vs 8MSolar's 8,414 kW. Renu offers a 5-year production guarantee; use pointed claims about guarantee effectiveness sparingly and only with a real basis.

named_competitors.name: Blue Raven Solar
named_competitors.notes: National/franchise competitor (SunPower subsidiary, HQ in Utah), not a local NC/VA company. Differentiation frame: local accountability and continuity vs. centralized national support. Blue Raven's appeal (single-day installs, $0 down, 18 months covered loan payments) should be acknowledged honestly, then contrasted with what happens after that introductory period.

rules: Never trash a competitor directly — acknowledge them as credible, let credentials/specifics do the persuading
Use third-party-sourced installation volume (kW) data when available — the most credible differentiator in the library
Frame competitor comparisons as fair, not a hit piece — this makes 8MSolar's stronger claims land harder
Address price questions directly (never dodge) and reframe toward long-term value
For national competitors, argue the relationship is structurally different (local accountability), not that national is 'bad'
